signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NZD/JPY trades under heavy pressure as JPY dominates G10 performance while NZD tags the bottom of the scoreboard. The G10 1W scorecard highlights a 2.204% spread between leader JPY (+1.231% avg) and laggard NZD (-0.974% avg across 4 pairs). TONA OIS at 0.98% vs RBNZ overnight rate at 2.75% maintains a carry differential favoring NZD, but market pricing for a potential 25bp BoJ rate increase at the upcoming meeting drives rapid yen repricing and carry unwinds. NZD/USD trades below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5836 while JPY data outperformance is reflected in a positive ESI index of +28.7. Options markets signal significant downside hedging in JPY crosses, and the BEER model flags NZD/JPY as cheap at z = -3.11σ (spot 89.82 vs fair value 93.79). Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; extreme G10 performance divergence and BoJ hike repricing favor continued downside. Catalyst: BoJ Rate Decision 18 Sep — market bias hawkish. Risk: BoJ holds policy rate unchanged and dampens hike expectations, forcing a rapid short-covering rally in JPY crosses.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Position Squeeze
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.09, holding well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 158.16, SMA50 159.98, SMA200 158.42). CFTC data shows CFTC JPY Leveraged Funds net short at -111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.18), marking an extreme spec short positioning condition that faces severe squeeze risk. 25d Risk Reversals print at -2.31, confirming heavy options market demand for JPY call / USD put downside protection. The cross-asset correlation between USD/JPY and VIX sits at +0.398 (z = +1.53σ), indicating a breakdown in standard safe-haven mechanics where JPY strength is driven by monetary policy repricing rather than equity risk-off. SOFR 3.64% vs TONA 0.98% maintains a +266bp carry advantage for USD, but carry demand is overridden by positioning liquidation ahead of the BoJ meeting. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; severe option put skew and spec short unwinding drive spot lower. Catalyst: BoJ Policy Meeting 18 Sep. Risk: Fed turns unexpectedly hawkish or US CPI surprises higher, reigniting carry demand above 158.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Policy Event + positioning Neutrality
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1628, positioned above its SMA20 (1.1625) and SMA50 (1.1525) but below the SMA200 (1.1638). ESTR OIS at 2.19% vs SOFR at 3.64% generates a +145bp carry spread favoring USD, while Fed policy rate at 3.75% vs ECB at 2.40% maintains a 135bp differential. CFTC positioning shows EUR Leveraged Funds net short at -52,784 (pctl 31, z -0.39), representing neutral positioning that offers little structural cushion against policy shifts. Option volatility reflects event pricing with 1M ATM IV at 5.0% vs HV30 at 4.2% (VRP +0.8%), while 25d Risk Reversals sit near neutral at -0.11. Market participants await the impending ECB rate decision and monetary policy statement today for fresh rate guidance. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; spot capped by SMA200 resistance ahead of central bank event risk. Catalyst: ECB Main Refinancing Rate decision and Press Conference today (12:15 / 12:45 UTC). Risk: ECB delivers an unexpectedly hawkish 25bp rate hike, driving a breakout above 1.1640.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7198, holding above its technical moving average cluster with SMA20 at 0.7159, SMA50 at 0.7060, and SMA200 at 0.6998. CFTC data reports Leveraged Funds net long at +50,250 contracts, placing positioning in the 94th percentile (z = +1.79) and signaling a stretched speculative long build. In contrast, Myfxbook retail sentiment shows 91% short / 9% long, creating an extreme institutional vs retail positioning divergence. RBA policy rate at 4.35% vs Fed at 3.75% provides a -60bp carry advantage favoring AUD (-71bp on AONIA vs SOFR basis), supporting spot demand. However, 25d Risk Reversals at -0.52 indicate mild options put skew as institutional desks hedge downside risk into extended territory. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional positioning momentum and carry advantage dominate retail fade effort. Catalyst: US CPI release today (12:30 UTC). Risk: Weak commodity demand or a broad USD rally pushes spot below SMA20 support at 0.7159.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility Complacency + Carry Support
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8114, sitting above its SMA20 (0.8073) and SMA50 (0.8088). Fed policy rate at 3.75% vs SNB at 0.00% creates a +375bp rate differential favoring USD, while SARON at -0.04% vs SOFR at 3.64% establishes a lucrative carry structure. FX options pricing reveals notable complacency, with 1M IV at 6.9% running below 30-day realized volatility at 7.8%, driving a negative Vol Risk Premium of -1.0%. CFTC Leveraged Funds maintain a net short CHF position of -12,346 contracts (pctl 16, z -0.93), showing moderate spec short bias against the Swiss franc. High oil prices and geopolitical headline risks provide underlying support for CHF safe-haven flows, conflicting with the structural carry deficit. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CHF; substantial carry differential supports spot above key moving averages. Catalyst: SNB Chairman Schlegel speech today (09:15 UTC) and upcoming SNB meeting 24 Sep. Risk: Acceleration in global risk aversion sparks sudden safe-haven CHF buying, pushing spot below 0.8070.
